@graph.name: Carton Case Packer
@graph.description: A carton packing machine, in secondary packaging, is a top-load case packer that collects finished folding cartons and places them into shipping cases in a counted, oriented pattern. TRF Industrial Automation packs cartons with TRFRapidpack and TRFOnepack. Which carton case packer fits your plant is defined mainly by your line setup and speed.

mainEntity.name: Does a Carton Packing Machine Need a Vision System?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only when carton position varies. TRFRapidpack packs with vision-guided delta robots when cartons arrive in a variable flow, or with indexed picking when they arrive in a controlled position, which is common when the cartoner discharges in a fixed index. The infeed design and the number of SKUs decide which approach fits, and TRF defines it in the application review.

mainEntity.name: Should Cartons Go Into a Shipping Case or Straight Onto the Pallet?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the channel. Cartons that ship in cases need a carton packing machine, while display-ready cartons that go directly onto the pallet need a carton palletizer. The two paths use different tooling, patterns and conveying, so decide early. Plants that do both can have the case packer, the conveying and the palletizer engineered by TRF as one project.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between an Integrated Case Packer and Separate Erecting, Packing and Sealing Machines?

acceptedAnswer.text: An integrated case packer erects the case, loads it and seals it in one coordinated machine, with one controls platform. Separate machines each need their own interfaces, controls and floor space. TRFOnepack is the integrated option, for applications of about 20 to 50 products per minute, and it can start standalone and later join a complete TRF end-of-line system.

mainEntity.name: How Many Products per Minute Can a Robotic Case Packer Run?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRFRapidpack is designed for applications of about 100 to 200 products per minute. TRF publishes application ranges, not machine speeds: actual capacity depends on the carton, the collation, the pick tool, the pack pattern and how cartons leave the cartoner, and TRF engineering validates it for each line before the design is closed.

mainEntity.name: Can Case Packing Equipment Integrate With My Existing Palletizer and Conveyors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each TRF case packing platform can run standalone or integrate with conveyors, case handling, palletizing and intralogistics as one end-of-line system. TRFIntraflow routes cases from one or several packing lines to a TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed palletizer, and interfaces with existing equipment are defined during project engineering. See end-of-line integration.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Case Packer and a Case Erector?

acceptedAnswer.text: A case erector forms an open case from a flat blank, and a case packer loads products into that case. TRF supplies case erecting only as part of an integrated solution: TRFOnepack erects, packs and seals in one machine, and end-of-line projects with TRFRapidpack include case forming and closing, so one partner answers for the flow from flat case to sealed case.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical ROI of Switching From Manual to Robotic Case Packing?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no typical figure, because payback depends on your plant. The estimate compares the installed cost of the system with the annual savings: operators packing cases per shift, shifts per day, local labor cost, output the cartoner gains when packing stops limiting it, cartons scuffed or crushed by handling and time saved at changeovers. A TRF Sales Engineer builds it with your data.
